trepidation

/trep-ih-DAY-shun/ - the stress falls on DAY · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Trepidation means nervous fear or uneasy apprehension about what is coming.

She saved the voicemail for two days, playing everything else first, and pressed it at last with trepidation.

Worked Example

The night before results day, Amaia cleaned an already clean kitchen. She had done the work — three drafts, two mock panels — and still her stomach dropped every time the email chimed. At nine she walked to the notice board with her coffee going cold in her hand, read her number twice, and only then noticed she had been holding her breath since the stairwell.

Trepidation is the exact word for that morning, because trepidation means fear or nervous apprehension — from Latin trepidare, to tremble: fear you can feel in your body while your head insists everything is fine. Panic has lost the argument entirely; trepidation still walks to the board, it just holds its breath on the way.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

apprehension: Apprehension is worry about what is coming — flat, mental, and containable; you can list your fears in an even voice. Trepidation is the same forward-looking fear with the body joined in: the tremble, the held breath, the stomach that drops. Apprehension sits in the head; trepidation shakes the hands.

jitters: The jitters are the informal, bodily name for pre-event nerves — bouncing knees before a recital, restless hands before an interview. Trepidation is the polished, formal word for the same trembling fear, the one that fits a written sentence. Same shaking; the register is the whole difference.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

composure: nerves held steady

nerve: boldness where fear would be

Where it sits · how completely fear stops you acting — unease → trepidation → terror

unease vs. trepidation: Unease is milder than trepidation — a low hum that something is off while you keep working; trepidation shakes in the body but still proceeds.

terror vs. trepidation: Terror goes further than trepidation — trepidation trembles and proceeds; terror has stopped proceeding altogether.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — trepid

Root — trepid: trembling (Latin trepidare)

Suffix — -ation

Suffix — -ation: the state of

Put it together

Put it together: Trepid- (trembling) + -ation (the state of) = the state of trembling. Latin trepidare described feet shifting and hands shaking; the word never lost the body — trepidation is fear you can measure in tremors.

One famous relative — already spoken for

One famous relative — already spoken for: Latin trepidare, 'to tremble,' survives in exactly one other common English word: intrepid, the fearless one who does not tremble — and this course teaches intrepid on its own card. Beyond that pair the root went quiet, so learn trepidation directly: fear with a tremble in it.

Strength Check

Word Choice

formal / self-aware

Trepidation is the polished word for stage-fright-grade nerves, often with a wry smile: with some trepidation, I opened the email. Apprehension is flatter; dread is heavier and surer of doom. Keep it apart from this unit's compunction, which aches over what you did, not what awaits you.
